prerequisites: Previous knowledge of fluid mechanics is required

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations and standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: Characteristic elements of a hydraulic machine.
General constructive characteristics and arrangements of different types of hydraulic turbomachinery.
Topic 2. Energy balance in hydraulic machines
Equation of conservation of total energy in fluid machines.
Equations of conservation of internal energy and mechanical energy in hydraulic machines.
Mechanical energy balances in pumps and turbines. Efficiencies.
Topic 3. General theory of hydraulic turbomachinery
Equation of conservation of angular momentum. Euler's equation.
Ideal one-dimensional theory of hydraulic turbomachinery.
Ideal two-dimensional theory of axial turbomachinery.
Dimensional analysis in turbomachinery. Relevant parameters.
Limitations of similarity theory in turbomachinery.
Topic 5. Centrifugal and axial pumps and fans
Design considerations for Francis and Kaplan turbines.
teaching_methods: Autonomous study (including theoretical content study and practical exercises)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment Test (Prueba de Evaluación Continua - PEC)

assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated as 0.80 * On-site exam score (CPP) + 0.15 * (max(Continuous Assessment Test score (CEC), CPP)) + 0.05 * Laboratory practicals score (CPL). A minimum final grade of 5 is required to pass the course. A minimum score of 4 on the on-site exam is required to consider the continuous assessment test score. Passing the laboratory practicals is mandatory, and generally requires having passed the on-site exam in the same academic year (with exceptions for students abroad or in the Canary/Balearic Islands who only need to have taken the exam).
